title: Portfolio Projects Overview
text:
Project 5 · Social Media Strategy
    Brand Humor in Crisis — Where's the Line?
    From an article, "Bunch of jerks: How brands can benefit by reappropriating insults" by Katherine M. Du, Keisha M. Cutright and Lingrui Zhou, my group assessed where it was appropriate to use humor in brand awareness. 
    
      Social Media Strategy
      Brand Voice
      Crisis Comms
    
    
      FrameworkIncluded real promotions, such as e.l.f beauty and the NFL, in order to include real life scenarios 
      Skills AppliedSocial strategy, brand tone analysis, crisis communication frameworks
      Key TakeawayHumor builds brand equity, but context, timing, and audience trust determine when it's a risk
    
  
  
    
      When humor works
      Brand not directly at fault · Audience has positive sentiment · Issue is lighthearted in nature
    
    
      When to stay serious
      Direct harm or controversy · Public trust is at stake · Audience is emotionally invested
    
    
      The takeaway
      Be cautious, understand where the line is before making a joke.

title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
This codebook documents the data preparation, descriptive summaries, visualization, and logistic regression modeling used to examine behavioral differences between users who converted and users who did not convert on the TRI website.
The goal is to identify which engagement behaviors are most strongly associated with conversion.






Note



This document is designed as a transparent analytical appendix. It shows how the data were prepared, how variables were defined, and how the models were estimated.

title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
Purpose
This section creates a simple behavioral comparison between users who converted and users who did not convert.

table_clean <- tibble(

  `Avg Scrolls` = c(26.3, 0.5),
  `Avg Form Starts` = c(34.0, 0.2)

title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
Data Source
The dataset used in this section was exported from BigQuery and saved locally as tri_logistic_clean.csv.

title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
Load Data

data <- read_csv("tri_logistic_clean.csv", skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)

title: TRI Logistic Regression Codebook
text:
Model 1: Behavioral Model
This model estimates the relationship between conversion and user behavior using log-transformed engagement measures plus device and traffic source controls.

model_improved <- glm(
  conversion ~ page_views_log + device_category + medium,
  data = data,
  family = "binomial"
)

    Year-long capstone project with the Trauma Resource Institute — using GA4, BigQuery, and Markov Chain models to identify which digital channels drive conversions.

      BigQuery
      Markov Chain
      Shapley Values
      R

      All 4 channels contribute equally (~20–22 credits each); longer journeys convert better
    
    
      Recommendation
      Use Markov as primary attribution model; invest across all channels, not just last-touch
